idiom_name: Active Job / Sidekiq job class + JSON arguments (Marshal/DRb between trusted processes)
implementation_notes: Ruby has a real object-graph codec, Marshal, and DRb uses it to ship arguments to a remote object - which makes "serialise the command and let the far side execute it" literal, and equally makes Marshal.load on untrusted bytes equivalent to code execution, because _dump/marshal_load/_load hooks run during loading. The safe, dominant realization is a job queue: Sidekiq and Active Job serialise the job CLASS NAME plus JSON arguments and the worker re-constantises the class and performs the job, so only JSON-native values and the worker's own loaded code cross the boundary. Reserve Marshal/DRb for processes you control over an authenticated, non-public channel.
code_sketch:
class RenderReportJob < ActiveJob::Base
  queue_as :render
  def perform(report_id)
    Renderer.new.render(report_id)
  end
end

RenderReportJob.perform_later(42)   # class name + JSON args go on the queue
# worker: ActiveJob::Base.execute("job_class" => "RenderReportJob", "arguments" => [42])
pitfalls: Marshal.load executes code: hook methods on any class the payload names run during loading, and DRb deserialises arguments from any client that can reach the URI - never expose DRb publicly and never Marshal.load queue payloads.

Active Job and Sidekiq only accept JSON-native arguments (String, numeric, boolean, nil, Symbol, Date/Time, Array, Hash with simple keys): passing a model, Proc or custom object raises on enqueue or silently loses type information.
A renamed or moved job class cannot be constantised by an old message, and keyword arguments must be declared explicitly - the worker's job class version is part of the wire contract.
